waterfalls.walk: Remain on the roadside-park side of M-28 for the verified waterfall view across the highway. There is no established public pedestrian crossing in these sources, and the waterfall-side path, under-ledge grotto and sandstone rim are NOT a certified visitor trail. Do not cross busy M-28 or climb to the falls based on this guide.
waterfalls.best: Spring snowmelt and rain bring stronger flow; summer can reduce the curtain to a thin trickle. View only where the roadside park is open and available.

waterfalls.kind: MDOT roadside park viewpoint across a busy highway
waterfalls.parking: Use MDOT's Scott Falls Roadside Park / H.J. Rathfoot State Roadside Park on the Lake Superior (north) side of M-28 near Au Train, only when the park entrance is open and the designated parking area is available. Alger County's recreation plan identifies this park and its waterfall view across the highway. Do not stop in a travel lane, on the bridge, or an undesignated shoulder. The natural waterfall GIS coordinate is NOT the roadside park entrance.
waterfalls.feature: A slender thread of water slipping over a sandstone ledge, visible across M-28 from a Lake Superior roadside park. A road-stop waterfall, not a creek hike.
waterfalls.further: The Alger County 2024 recreation plan, page 35, describes parking and a waterfall view across the highway. MDOT's April 21, 2026 announcement lists Scott Falls Roadside Park and notes delayed spring reopening due to snow; it also describes roadside parks as often seasonal, closing in late October. Neither establishes the park's current October 31 opening. No pedestrian crossing, waterfall-side trail, safe grotto approach, roadside shoulder or exact parking GPS has been independently approved.

waterfalls.decision: Choose a short park-side viewpoint if the MDOT roadside park is open. Do not cross M-28 to the falls or use a shoulder pull-off as a substitute if the park is closed.

waterfalls.parking: Small eastern Miners Beach lot off Miners Beach Road via Miners Castle Road; larger western Miners Beach lot offers a longer sandy walk.
waterfalls.feature: A petite Lake Superior shoreline cascade over sculpted rock, with a very different experience than the inland Miners Falls trail.
waterfalls.further: Choose the beach route only when waves, sand and steps permit safe access. Never follow the waterfall coordinate by car.
waterfalls.manager: National Park Service · Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore
waterfalls.season: Small creek flow can nearly disappear in dry periods; Lake Superior surf is a separate access hazard.

publicAccess.description: An NPS-listed public waterfall at Miners Beach. Leashed pets allowed. Beach sand, stairs, shoreline rock and wave conditions limit access.

landManager.description: National Park Service · Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore

parking.description: Small eastern Miners Beach lot off Miners Beach Road via Miners Castle Road; larger western Miners Beach lot offers a longer sandy walk.

trail.description: From the small east-end Miners Beach lot, take the designated staircase down to sand, then walk a few hundred yards right along the shore toward the cliff where the creek drops into Lake Superior.

location.description: Published geographic location for Elliot Falls, not a parking point

waterfalls.name: Manido Falls
waterfalls.walk: Signed Presque Isle River East/West River trails link waterfalls. DNR park map lists the West River Trail at 1 mile and East River Trail at 1.4 miles; neither is a certified walk distance specifically to Manido.
waterfalls.best: Spring runoff and hardwood autumn color; bedrock is slippery when wet.
waterfalls.access: Public Michigan DNR state park scenic corridor. Only signed viewing trails and overlooks are appropriate; stairs, uneven rocks and road conditions vary.
waterfalls.note: Michigan GIS spells the site 'Mannido Falls' (state feature 92); DNR's park map uses Manido. It is one of three separate Presque Isle River waterfalls.
waterfalls.parking: Presque Isle River Scenic Site designated state park parking near West/East River trail access; use the official Porcupine Mountains map for M-519 and South Boundary Road routes.
waterfalls.feature: An intermediate cascade between Manabezho and Nawadaha, experienced as part of the Presque Isle River walking circuit.
waterfalls.further: Plan the three waterfall viewpoints as one walking outing rather than three independent parking stops. Winter roads and platforms may close.
waterfalls.manager: Michigan DNR · Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
waterfalls.season: High river flow changes safe viewing positions; winter ice never makes cliff-edge approaches safe.

publicAccess.description: Public Michigan DNR state park scenic corridor. Only signed viewing trails and overlooks are appropriate; stairs, uneven rocks and road conditions vary.

landManager.description: Michigan DNR · Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park

parking.description: Presque Isle River Scenic Site designated state park parking near West/East River trail access; use the official Porcupine Mountains map for M-519 and South Boundary Road routes.

trail.description: Signed Presque Isle River East/West River trails link waterfalls. DNR park map lists the West River Trail at 1 mile and East River Trail at 1.4 miles; neither is a certified walk distance specifically to Manido.

location.description: Published geographic location for Manido Falls, not a parking point

waterfalls.name: Upper Hungarian Falls
waterfalls.walk: From the Golf Course Road shoulder near the Hungarian Falls sign, follow the old gated access road on foot approximately 400 yards toward the pond and upper falls. This is a rustic route, not a paved accessible path.
waterfalls.best: Spring snowmelt, after sustained rain, and hardwood color; no live water-flow measurement.
waterfalls.access: Keweenaw Land Trust states that its upper 10-acre nature area is open to the public year-round for nonmotorized visits. Golf Course Road is not fully plowed in winter.
waterfalls.note: This is the shorter, easier access into the Hungarian Falls complex. The historic dam/pond is not a designated swimming facility; water and edges require caution.
waterfalls.parking: Shoulder of Golf Course Road near the Hungarian Falls Nature Area sign, about 0.5 mi uphill from 6th Street in Tamarack City. KLT's parking reference: 47.173159, -88.444743. Never drive the old gated woods road.
waterfalls.feature: A public land-trust preserve at the top of the Dover Creek gorge with the historic dam, pond and upper falls.
waterfalls.further: The upper waterfall is on the KLT preserve; much of the lower gorge is on Michigan state land, with private parcels nearby. Do not assume all visible paths are public.
waterfalls.manager: Keweenaw Land Trust · upper 10-acre nature area
waterfalls.decision: Pick the upper falls when you want the shortest officially described walk and a look at the Keweenaw Fault landscape without committing to the steep lower gorge.

landManager.description: KLT conserves and opens the upper 10 acres to public nonmotorized visits

publicAccess.description: KLT publishes year-round public hiking access; winter road conditions change

parking.description: KLT Golf Course Road roadside parking: 47.173159, -88.444743; old gated drive not for vehicles

trail.description: KLT brochure: walk about 400 yards along rough former access road to upper nature area

location.description: Michigan state GIS source waterfall point 134, distinct from parking

parkingLocation.label: Hungarian Falls shared Golf Course Road shoulder arrival
parkingLocation.certainty: Official map reference, road is seasonal and unplowed in winter; do not enter the gated woods road

waterfalls.name: Lower Hungarian Falls
waterfalls.walk: From the KLT-signed Golf Course Road access, follow the rough former drive toward the gorge, take the downstream/left-side path, and use the marked public trail corridor. The entire gorge traverse is roughly two miles, with steep, eroded cliffside sections and no protective fences.
waterfalls.best: Spring melt or rain when the lower cascade carries water; roots and ledges may be slippery even in dry weather.
waterfalls.access: Keweenaw Land Trust describes public hiking throughout the gorge, with its upper parcel and a large Michigan state-owned section; its mapped brochure is essential because neighboring parcels are private.
waterfalls.note: The lower fall is NOT the easy upper KLT preserve access. Routes descend a steep gorge, and maps should not be mistaken for a guaranteed safe trail surface.
waterfalls.parking: Use the KLT-published Golf Course Road shoulder parking, near 47.173159, -88.444743. In winter park only where legally plowed; KLT says most of Golf Course Road is unplowed.
waterfalls.feature: A lower gorge waterfall reached by rustic trails, with steep cliffs, exposed rock and a distinct visitor decision from Upper Hungarian Falls.
waterfalls.further: KLT's ownership map colors its 10-acre upper preserve, state lands and neighboring private parcels differently. Remain on public paths and do not improvise gorge-crossings.
waterfalls.manager: Michigan DNR-owned gorge parcels; Keweenaw Land Trust manages upper access parcel (check parcel map)
waterfalls.decision: Choose the lower waterfall only if you want a challenging gorge walk; otherwise use the signed upper preserve path. Do not recommend cliff-edge shortcuts.

landManager.description: KLT mapped brochure distinguishes state-owned lower gorge, upper KLT land and private neighbors

publicAccess.description: KLT publishes public hiking from Tamarack City/Golf Course Road to the gorge

parking.description: KLT roadside shoulder parking and winter plowing restrictions

trail.description: KLT gorge trail map: roughly two miles for the system, strenuous lower sections

location.description: Michigan state GIS waterfall point 130, not trailhead

parkingLocation.label: Hungarian Falls shared Golf Course Road shoulder arrival
parkingLocation.certainty: Official map reference, road is seasonal and unplowed in winter; do not enter the gated woods road

waterfalls.name: Fumee Falls
waterfalls.place: Dickinson County · east of Iron Mountain
waterfalls.walk: Begin at the Fumee Falls Roadside Park parking area on the north side of US-2; a short stairway/boardwalk approach leads toward the upper creek tiers. Use only maintained visitor paths, not highway shoulders.
waterfalls.best: Spring melt or after recent rain; flow can be thin during dry summer weeks.
waterfalls.access: MDOT publishes Fumee Falls Roadside Park as a state visitor facility, but most MDOT roadside parks close for the season October 29, 2026. Check this specific park's open/gated status before planning a stop.
waterfalls.note: Unlike long hikes, this waterfall is a brief roadside stop. A small three-tier fall is not a guaranteed strong-flow destination in dry periods.
waterfalls.parking: Fumee Falls Roadside Park on the north side of US-2, approximately six miles east of Iron Mountain. Follow park signage and do not enter closed gates or park in the traffic lane.
waterfalls.feature: A compact three-tier creek fall reached from an established MDOT roadside park beside US-2.
waterfalls.further: MDOT's October 15, 2026 notice says most parks close October 29; that is a seasonal facility warning, not a live report of Fumee's gate. Check before driving.
waterfalls.manager: Michigan Department of Transportation · Fumee Falls Roadside Park
waterfalls.decision: Best for a brief, signed-roadside waterfall stop on a US-2 drive; choose other falls for a long hiking day.

landManager.description: Official MDOT Pure Michigan byways driving guide identifies Fumee Falls Roadside Park

publicAccess.description: MDOT lists roadside parks as public travel recreation facilities

parking.description: Official Fumee Falls roadside park, US-2; observe posted gated access

trail.description: Regional Fumee Falls guide identifies short boardwalk/stair access to tiers

location.description: Michigan waterfall GIS ID 6, location is fall not visitor parking

waterfalls.name: Bridalveil Falls
waterfalls.place: Miners Castle / Miners Beach, Alger County
waterfalls.walk: No maintained trail reaches Bridalveil Falls itself. For a distant view, walk from the Miners Castle parking lot to its lower overlook (stairs and a steep grade), or use the short west-end Miners Beach boardwalk for a shore view. A concession-operated boat tour gives the most complete cliffside view.
waterfalls.best: Snowmelt and spring rains; the creek can be a trickle in dry summer weather. Sightlines and boat sailings depend on conditions.
waterfalls.access: Publicly viewable from NPS-managed Miners Castle and Miners Beach vantage points, or from an authorized sightseeing boat. Do not route hikers to the waterfall brink, cliff base or North Country Trail.
waterfalls.note: The signature view is from Lake Superior. Shore viewpoints are distant; an NPS viewpoint does not guarantee visible flow on a given day.
waterfalls.parking: Miners Castle lot at the end of Miners Castle Road (H-11) for lower overlook; or west-end Miners Beach lot, reached via Miners Beach Road off H-11. These are visitor arrival areas, not the falls coordinates.
waterfalls.feature: A seasonal cliffside ribbon falling toward Lake Superior; the decision is where to view it, not which trail to the falls to take.
waterfalls.further: There is no safe, maintained land route directly to the waterfall. The lower Miners Castle overlook has stairs and a steep incline; the west Miners Beach boardwalk is wheelchair-accessible to its platform. The falls may be nearly dry.
waterfalls.manager: National Park Service · Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore
waterfalls.decision: Choose a boat tour for the full waterfall-and-cliff view; Miners Castle for a distant overlook; Miners Beach for a gentler viewpoint. Do not attempt a direct waterfall hike.

landManager.description: NPS confirms Bridalveil is inside Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore and identifies official viewing options

publicAccess.description: NPS lists viewing from the water, distant Miners Castle lower overlook and west end of Miners Beach; not from North Country Trail

parking.description: NPS Miners Castle parking at end of H-11 and signed scenic overlooks; alternative Miners Beach parking documented by NPS

trail.description: NPS Miners Beach west-end boardwalk to shore overlook. No maintained trail to the falls itself; lower Miners Castle overlook has stairs.

location.description: Alger County Chamber publishes approximate geographic waterfall coordinates 46.5087, -86.5233; not a parking point

waterfalls.name: Rapid River Falls (Delta County)
waterfalls.place: Masonville Township / Rapid River, Delta County
waterfalls.walk: From the signed day-use parking area, follow the county's developed viewing walkway. The county lists additional nature trails but does not publish a measured parking-to-waterfall walking distance.
waterfalls.best: Spring runoff over limestone shelves and fall foliage; no current water-flow measurement is supplied.
waterfalls.access: Delta County publishes year-round day-use operation, but that does not verify the gate, parking or walkway is currently open. The county assesses overall park accessibility at 1 of 5 despite an accessible viewing walkway.
waterfalls.note: Small limestone cascades and interesting karst landscape, not a tall cliff plunge. Stay on designated viewing areas; undeveloped ground contains possible sinkholes.
waterfalls.parking: Rapid River Falls County Park, 13149 S 15, Rapid River MI 49878. Follow signed park access from US-41 near the Rapid River crossing; park only in the designated visitor area.
waterfalls.feature: An 80-acre county park where the Rapid River spills across limestone shelves beside a developed viewing walkway.
waterfalls.further: Accessible waterfall walkway does not mean accessible parking, all facilities or every trail. The county rates overall accessibility 1/5 and flags needed parking improvements.
waterfalls.manager: Delta County Parks and Recreation
waterfalls.decision: A 20–45 minute river-and-karst stop on the US-41 corridor; ideal for a short waterfall break rather than a long hiking day.
waterfalls.locationQuality: GNIS-derived geographic waterfall point, not a parking or trailhead coordinate.
waterfalls.sourceDisambiguation: Do not match by name to Michigan GIS waterfall object 60 at 46.627099,-89.668576 in the western U.P.; the Delta County waterfall lies near 46.021667,-86.983333.

landManager.description: County park authority identifies the 80-acre park and day-use recreation.

publicAccess.description: County 2026–2030 recreation plan lists public year-round day-use park and a waterfall viewing walkway.

parking.description: Delta County township directory lists Dutch Mill / Rapid River Falls Park at 13149 S 15, Rapid River; official plan describes signed US-41 approach.

trail.description: County plan documents developed waterfall walkway and nature trails, without measurable approach length; accessibility rated 1/5 overall.

location.description: GNIS-derived Delta County Rapid River Falls coordinate 46.0216667,-86.9833333; not park entrance or western namesake.

waterfalls.name: Haven Falls
waterfalls.walk: From the designated Haven Falls Park parking area, walk a short distance through the roadside picnic grounds toward the waterfall behind the park. The falls are visible from the parking area; no backcountry trail is necessary.
waterfalls.best: Spring snowmelt typically brings more water to the short Haven Creek cascade; low-flow periods can be quiet.
waterfalls.access: Haven Falls Park is a public county-road-commission roadside park. County recreation inventory lists partial—not universal—accessibility; confirm restrooms, surfaces and seasonal conditions before visiting.
waterfalls.note: Haven Falls Park sits opposite Lac La Belle. The county's accessibility assessment of 2 means some facilities meet guidelines, not that every route is wheelchair accessible.
waterfalls.parking: Haven Falls Park on Gay–Lac La Belle Road, near Lac La Belle. From US-41 take Lac La Belle Road about 4.5 miles to the fork, then right about 0.5 mile to the park on the right.
waterfalls.feature: A small waterfall spills over Keweenaw conglomerate into Haven Creek behind a public picnic park near Lac La Belle.
waterfalls.further: There is no reason to follow a private driveway or scramble upstream to see this waterfall. Stay on established public park surfaces.
waterfalls.manager: Keweenaw County Road Commission (Haven Falls Park)
waterfalls.decision: Best short stop for travelers wanting a picnic, restrooms and waterfall together, rather than a remote forest hike.

landManager.description: 2025–2029 Keweenaw County Recreation Plan identifies Haven Falls Park as owned by the Keweenaw County Road Commission.

publicAccess.description: County recreation inventory describes an available roadside public park; no private approach is required.

parking.description: Visit Keweenaw provides signed road directions to Haven Falls Park and places the falls behind its park parking area.

trail.description: Visitor authority describes a short walk inside the park and waterfall visible from the car. No surveyed trail length is stated.

location.description: Michigan geographic waterfall feature 138 (47.382887, -88.025673), not a surveyed parking entrance.

waterfalls.name: Eagle River Falls
waterfalls.walk: Park at Eagle River Bridge Park just off M-26 and use the designated pedestrian bridge to view the waterfall; the walk from parking to bridge is only a short stroll, not a riverbank hike.
waterfalls.best: Spring melt often makes this Eagle River gorge especially dramatic; winter ice may cover parts of the cascades without establishing safe footing.
waterfalls.access: MDOT owns the publicly described Eagle River Bridge Park. View from the established pedestrian bridge, not from the old industrial dam, highway bridge roadway or gorge edge.
waterfalls.note: Historic fuse-company dam remains influence the waterfall appearance. From the visitor bridge, turn around to see the historic two-arched M-26 timber road bridge.
waterfalls.kind: MDOT roadside park and pedestrian bridge
waterfalls.parking: Eagle River Bridge Park beside the township hall, 5055 M-26 in Eagle River. Use the small signed visitor parking area off M-26; do not park on the bridge shoulder.
waterfalls.feature: An old copper-country industrial waterfall and dam in a deep Eagle River gorge, viewed from a public pedestrian bridge beside the timber M-26 bridge.
waterfalls.further: The pedestrian bridge is a viewing structure, not permission to access the historic dam or descend into the gorge. Ice and high water change hazards.
waterfalls.manager: Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT), Eagle River Bridge Park
waterfalls.decision: The best easy Keweenaw stop for a waterfall view framed by industrial history and an unusual timber arch bridge.

landManager.description: 2025–2029 Keweenaw County Recreation Plan lists Eagle River Bridge Park as owned by MDOT.

publicAccess.description: County identifies a public roadside park by the township hall with an established view of Eagle River Falls.

parking.description: Visit Keweenaw directs visitors to the small parking area on the right after crossing M-26 bridge in Eagle River.

trail.description: Visit Keweenaw explicitly describes the pedestrian bridge from parking to the Lower Eagle River Falls viewing position.

location.description: Michigan waterfall GIS feature 142 at the falls, not a parking GPS point.

waterfalls.name: Silver River Falls
waterfalls.place: M-26 east of Eagle Harbor, Keweenaw County
waterfalls.walk: The Keweenaw visitor brochure describes a rustic pull-off south of the M-26 Silver River bridge and a short path on the north side. That route would require an at-grade highway crossing, which has not been independently confirmed as a safe legal pedestrian approach.
waterfalls.best: Spring flow over the stepped Silver River bedrock; wet rocks and ice can make streamside footing hazardous.
waterfalls.access: A county recreation inventory identifies Silver River Falls Park as a public waterfall location, but highway crossing design and exact legal visitor approach are unresolved. Do not use this page as driving or pedestrian routing advice.
waterfalls.note: Research guide only. Park ownership is identified in an older county land-use plan as MDOT, while the 2025–2029 county recreation plan lists the site but gives no current crossing guidance.
waterfalls.kind: MDOT roadside park (historic county ownership record)
waterfalls.parking: A Keweenaw visitor brochure identifies a rustic parking area south of M-26 at the Silver River bridge, about 4.5 miles east of Eagle Harbor. Arrival and safe pedestrian crossing remain unverified.
waterfalls.feature: A tiered Silver River waterfall near an M-26 roadside park, still awaiting a documented safe walking connection from visitor parking.
waterfalls.further: Do not cross M-26 or enter the river gorge solely on these directions. Confirm legal pedestrian access and any roadwork with the responsible road authority.
waterfalls.manager: MDOT per county land-use inventory; updated park oversight not separately confirmed
waterfalls.decision: Keep this as a map research stop for now; Haven or Eagle River offers a better documented arrival and viewing route.

landManager.description: County land-use inventory identifies Silver River Falls Park as an MDOT roadside park; current oversight has not been reconfirmed.

publicAccess.description: County identifies Silver River Falls Park, but a designated pedestrian crossing is not established by the recreation plan.

parking.description: Visit Keweenaw waterfall brochure reports a south-side M-26 parking area.

trail.description: Visitor brochure locates the path north of M-26, opposite the parking area. Safe/legal crossing must be resolved first.

location.description: State of Michigan GIS waterfall feature 146, distinct from roadside parking or access point.

waterfalls.name: Pinnacle Falls
waterfalls.place: Yellow Dog River / Big Bay, Marquette County
waterfalls.walk: Approximately one mile each way from the preserve parking area, on a steep, rugged foot trail descending into the Yellow Dog River gorge; use the posted trail and its mid-route interpretive sign. Expect a strenuous climb back to the car.
waterfalls.best: Spring runoff may make the waterfall stronger; fall colors the red-pine and hardwood gorge. This is seasonal character, not a live flow forecast.
waterfalls.access: Pinnacle Falls Preserve is a 280-acre Yellow Dog Watershed Preserve protected property; the owner lists hiking as an allowed use. Stay on the established preserve foot trail and respect preserve rules. No current same-day road or trail-open guarantee.
waterfalls.note: This is the separate Pinnacle Falls Preserve, not the Yellow Dog River Community Forest waterfall trailhead on County Road 510. The preserve's designated parking entrance is reached by a different sequence of roads.
waterfalls.parking: Small signed Pinnacle Falls Preserve parking area at the end of the remote access two-track from County Road AAA, reached via CR-550 and CR-510 from Marquette/Big Bay. The preserve owner publishes turn-by-turn guidance; do not drive to the waterfall coordinate. Road surface, winter clearance and two-track passability must be checked before driving.
waterfalls.feature: A rugged descent into a Yellow Dog River gorge where a wooded rock pinnacle towers above a roughly 25–30-foot cascade.
waterfalls.further: The two-track and final descent can be difficult. Do not use the feature coordinate for driving, expect an accessible path or assume the seasonal road has been maintained.
waterfalls.manager: Yellow Dog Watershed Preserve · Pinnacle Falls Preserve (conservation easement held by The Nature Conservancy)
waterfalls.decision: Choose Pinnacle for a substantial wooded gorge hike and the river's geologic story. Choose Wagner or Fumee instead if you need a short developed visitor path.

landManager.description: Owner states it purchased 40 acres in 2003 and received 240 more acres in 2017, creating the current 280-acre preserve; The Nature Conservancy holds the conservation easement.

publicAccess.description: Preserve expressly permits hiking, fishing, birding and other non-motorized activities; camping and motorized use have restrictions.

parking.description: Owner describes small parking at the signed end of a road/two-track from CR-AAA via CR-550/CR-510. Exact parking coordinates are not independently surveyed.

trail.description: Owner describes roughly one mile of steep rugged trail, a midpoint sign, and an approach from the north to the falls.

location.description: Michigan state GIS waterfall feature 155 is a falls coordinate, corroborated within 11 meters by independent USGS V2 hydrography; neither supplies an entrance coordinate.

hydrography.description: 2020 USGS V2 NHDPlus COMID 12025618, linked to Michigan GIS ID 155 by independent spatial/name match. Not an access source.

waterfalls.name: Yellow Dog Falls
waterfalls.place: Big Bay / Yellow Dog River Community Forest
waterfalls.walk: Follow the established forest trail from the County Road 510 bridge parking area on the south side of the Yellow Dog River, downstream toward the falls. Landowner estimates about 0.75 mile to the first falls; a published geological field guide describes roughly 0.5 mile to Yellow Dog Falls. Treat mileage as approximate and return on the signed route.
waterfalls.best: Spring snowmelt and autumn forest color. Seasonal patterns, not a current flow or trail-surface observation.
waterfalls.access: Yellow Dog Watershed Preserve owns and protects the public 688-acre Community Forest. The established nonmotorized trail leads from the signed bridge-side entrance into the waterfall corridor. Do not cross into downstream private parcels or use river fords as an informal shortcut.
waterfalls.note: Yellow Dog Falls (also called Hills Falls) is reached from the Community Forest parking area at the CR-510 Yellow Dog River bridge. Pinnacle Falls is a different protected property with a separate two-track arrival.
waterfalls.parking: Yellow Dog River Community Forest's primary public parking and trailhead immediately south of the Yellow Dog River bridge on County Road 510. From CR-550 follow CR-510, turn left after about 2.6 miles to stay on dirt CR-510 at the AAA junction, continue about 3.9 miles and cross the river; landowner directs visitors to the lot on the left.
waterfalls.feature: A series of forested river drops and rock ledges reached by a maintained public trail from the County Road 510 bridge, not the remote Pinnacle Falls entrance.
waterfalls.further: Allow extra time for the unpaved CR-510 approach and check road conditions. Do not assume wheelchair access, a guaranteed winter-plowed lot, cellphone coverage, safe swimming, or live flow measurements.
waterfalls.manager: Yellow Dog Watershed Preserve · Yellow Dog River Community Forest (688 acres)
waterfalls.decision: Choose Yellow Dog Falls for a public forest trail and a series of river cascades. Choose Pinnacle Falls for a much more remote, steep gorge outing from a different signed road and parking area.

landManager.description: Yellow Dog Watershed Preserve confirms ownership and monitoring of the 688-acre Yellow Dog River Community Forest, held for public nonmotorized recreation.

publicAccess.description: Landowner explicitly documents public entry at the CR-510 Yellow Dog River bridge and an established trail into the waterfall area.

parking.description: Landowner supplies the CR-550 to CR-510 to dirt CR-510 route and parking/trailhead south of the river bridge. No surveyed lot coordinate is invented.

trail.description: Landowner confirms signed primary access and trail to multiple waterfalls, reporting roughly three-quarters of a mile to the first falls. A geology field guide gives about a half-mile to Yellow Dog Falls.

location.description: AIPG geologic field trip identifies Yellow Dog Falls at N46°43.720', W87°42.403'; independent waterfall documentation corroborates the falls point near 46.72865, -87.70674. This is not a parking pin.

waterfalls.name: Kakabika Falls
waterfalls.place: Cisco Branch Ontonagon River / near Marenisco
waterfalls.walk: From the small signed falls parking area beside County Road 527, follow the short riverside footpath along the Cisco Branch Ontonagon River. The U.S. Forest Service calls the trail short and not difficult; exact accessible grade or distance is not certified.
waterfalls.best: Spring snowmelt or following recent rain; low water reveals the bedrock S-turns.
waterfalls.access: An Ottawa National Forest recreation destination with a published public trail and small parking area; check seasonal road and trail conditions. Neither live opening nor wheelchair accessibility has been verified.
waterfalls.note: The sign and lot are on County Road 527. Do not drive to the state GIS waterfall coordinate or assume the trail extends farther downstream onto private land.
waterfalls.parking: Approach County Road 527 from US-2 between Watersmeet and Marenisco. The federal recreation listing identifies the Bessemer Ranger District, and U.P. Travel specifies the signed parking area before the bridge. Use the small designated lot, not the road shoulder.
waterfalls.feature: On the Cisco Branch Ontonagon River, a succession of bends and rock ledges forms an unusual S-shaped waterfall instead of one vertical plunge.
waterfalls.further: Do not confuse Kakabika Falls in Michigan with Kakabeka Falls in Ontario. Forest conditions and road maintenance can change, especially after a storm or freeze.
waterfalls.manager: U.S. Forest Service · Ottawa National Forest, Bessemer Ranger District
waterfalls.decision: Best for a short, quieter forest stop when you want unusual river geology without committing to a long gorge hike.

landManager.description: Federal Recreation.gov visitor listing identifies Ottawa National Forest and Bessemer Ranger District

publicAccess.description: Forest Service lists Kakabika Falls as a recreation site with a public hiking trail

parking.description: UP Travel specifies signed visitor lot beside County Road 527 before crossing the river bridge

trail.description: Forest Service describes a short, not difficult walking trail to the river falls

location.description: Michigan GIS Waterfalls layer feature 21; marks falls, not public parking

waterfalls.name: Interstate Falls
waterfalls.walk: The landowner's published route is a 0.7-mile out-and-back woodland walk to the Montreal River lookout. It is a natural-surface trail, not a barrier-free platform or a drive-up waterfall.
waterfalls.best: Spring runoff and autumn hardwoods; winter requires checking trail and road surface.
waterfalls.access: The documented public route begins in the Town of Kimball, Iron County, Wisconsin. The river itself forms the Michigan–Wisconsin state line; the map point is NOT a legal Michigan-side trail or an entrance.
waterfalls.note: Do not follow a Michigan riverside two-track or an improvised route to the mapped waterfall. The Wisconsin conservation-area entrance is the documented public approach.
waterfalls.parking: In Wisconsin, head north from Hurley on Highway 51, turn west onto US-2, continue approximately 0.6 mile, then turn onto Center Drive and drive about 0.2 mile to the signed Interstate Falls trailhead. Do not use the waterfall coordinate as parking.
waterfalls.feature: An 18-foot plunge on the Montreal River, which divides Michigan from Wisconsin, protected by a town-owned conservation parcel on the Wisconsin bank.
waterfalls.further: A U.P. waterfall on the state boundary is not necessarily accessed from Michigan. This visitor route is a Wisconsin-side walk, with dogs leashed under Town of Kimball rules.
waterfalls.manager: Town of Kimball, Iron County, Wisconsin · conserved through Northwoods Land Trust
waterfalls.decision: Best for a short border-country woodland walk and a river-gorge view; plan the arrival from the Wisconsin side, not Ironwood's Michigan roads.

landManager.description: Northwoods Land Trust records the land purchase and 2016 conveyance to the Town of Kimball, Wisconsin

publicAccess.description: Town-owned conservation area explicitly open for public waterfall viewing

parking.description: Published Wisconsin arrival instructions via US-2 and Center Drive to the trailhead

trail.description: Landowner describes 0.7-mile out-and-back trail to Interstate Falls

location.description: Michigan GIS Waterfalls layer feature 35, a waterfall point on the Montreal River boundary

waterfalls.name: Superior Falls
waterfalls.walk: Signed upper and lower waterfall viewing paths from the utility-side public parking area. The lower gorge path is steep, rocky or uneven and may be dangerous when wet or icy; a shorter upper overlook is the safer alternative for some visitors. Wisconsin tourism describes 0.5–1 mile of visitor walking, depending on route.
waterfalls.best: Spring runoff and autumn color; regulated hydroelectric releases mean appearance varies and cannot be forecast from a seasonal label.
waterfalls.access: Public access is described by a regional access inventory and Wisconsin tourism guidance on the MICHIGAN side of the Montreal River. The land is adjoining an active hydroelectric station operated by Northern States Power / Xcel Energy. Follow the signed visitor paths only; no crossing to an assumed Wisconsin-bank access is needed.
waterfalls.note: This is not Interstate Falls, farther upstream on the same border river. Superior Falls visitors reach a signed utility-side gravel parking approach on Michigan land; the steep lower gorge is optional.
waterfalls.parking: From US-2 in Wisconsin take Highway 122 north approximately 4.2 miles, cross the state line into Michigan, continue roughly 0.5 mile and turn left onto the signed gravel access road for the utility-side parking area. The mapped waterfall is not the parking entrance.
waterfalls.feature: A series of red-sandstone drops on the Montreal River near Lake Superior, beside a working hydroelectric plant and the Michigan–Wisconsin border.
waterfalls.further: Never approach the powerhouse, dam structures or fenced/posted areas. The access inventory warns the lower trail is steep and dangerous when icy or wet. Road and trail opening are not verified in real time.
waterfalls.manager: Northern States Power Company (Xcel Energy), Superior Falls Hydroelectric Project P-2587
waterfalls.decision: Choose the signed upper overlook for a shorter viewing stop. Consider the steeper lower gorge only with suitable footwear and dry conditions; this is not an accessible paved trail.

landManager.description: FERC identifies Northern States Power as the applicant and utility operator for Superior Falls Hydroelectric Project P-2587; county public access study describes Xcel-owned adjoining property.

publicAccess.description: Bayfield County regional public access inventory describes Michigan-side visitor access, a public parking area, benches and trails near Superior Falls; utility facilities and posted restrictions remain off limits.

parking.description: Travel Wisconsin publishes the Highway 122 approach, Michigan state-line crossing, signed left-turn gravel road and visitor parking area.

trail.description: Public access study lists upper/lower scenic paths and warns the lower gorge descent is steep and potentially dangerous when wet or icy; tourism listing describes rough 0.5–1 mile walking.

location.description: Michigan state geographic waterfall feature 50 locates the falls, distinct from public parking. USGS Falls/Rapids V2 name-matched point lies approximately 2 m away; neither supplies a legal route.

waterfalls.name: Horseshoe Falls
waterfalls.walk: The operator lists a 400-foot walk from its on-site parking area to the falls, through the gift-shop grounds. This is a maintained paid attraction, not a wilderness hike.
waterfalls.best: Spring and summer during its advertised early May–mid October operating season. Springs feed the waterfall, so it can retain flow when nearby small streams are low.
waterfalls.access: Privately owned, ticketed waterfall attraction. The operator describes leashed-pet access and an accessible visitor route. Verify specific mobility needs and today's operation directly with the business.
waterfalls.note: This is separate from the federally managed Pictured Rocks trails. An admission ticket and seasonal operating calendar apply; do not confuse Horseshoe Falls with the closed Munising Falls trail.
waterfalls.parking: Official visitor parking at Horseshoe Falls & Gift Shop, 602 Bell Avenue, Munising, Michigan 49862. Route to the street address, not the waterfall GIS coordinates.
waterfalls.feature: A spring-fed waterfall within maintained gardens, with a trout pond and a family scavenger hunt; an easy paid alternative to a long backcountry waterfall hike.
waterfalls.further: As of October 27, 2026, the operator advertises early May through mid-October seasonal hours, usually 9 AM–7 PM during its season. Do not assume the grounds are open outside those dates. Prices and hours can change.
waterfalls.manager: Horseshoe Falls & Gift Shop (private operator), Munising
waterfalls.decision: Choose this when a short maintained walk, family activities or a more predictable spring-fed cascade matters more than a remote forest hike. It is not a free state or national park stop.

landManager.description: City of Munising recreation plan explicitly identifies Horseshoe Falls as a privately owned, admission-charging attraction accessed from Bell Avenue.

publicAccess.description: Munising Visitor's Bureau confirms the publicly offered visitor entrance is private and admission-based, with a gentle walking path.

parking.description: The private operator lists the arrival address 602 Bell Avenue, Munising; parking is on its own grounds. No lot coordinate is fabricated.

trail.description: The operator states the fall is approximately 400 feet from its parking lot and describes its accessible visitor route; not a certified ADA site-specific audit.

location.description: Michigan GIS mapped waterfall feature #197 is at 46.402894, -86.642575. This is the falls, not the parking lot; USGS hydro reference is 107 m away.

waterfalls.name: Greenstone Falls
waterfalls.walk: From the signed Little Carp River Road trailhead, cross the first bridge at Overlooked Falls and continue along the Little Carp River Trail toward Greenstone. Plan roughly a 2-mile out-and-back excursion; use the park trail map for current alignment and do not expect a paved path.
waterfalls.best: Spring rain and snowmelt strengthen this relatively low cascade; autumn adds hardwood color.
waterfalls.access: Public park trail on state-managed land, reached from Little Carp River Road off South Boundary Road. Road and trail access may change seasonally; no year-round vehicle access is implied.
waterfalls.note: Greenstone is a small, shaded forest cascade, not a tall vertical drop. The trailhead also serves nearby Overlooked Falls; do not confuse the first bridge cascade with the Greenstone destination farther downstream.
waterfalls.parking: Park only at the marked Little Carp River Trailhead at the end of Little Carp River Road, reached from South Boundary Road in Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park. The falls coordinate is not the lot.
waterfalls.feature: A secluded Little Carp River cascade, reached by a forest walk from the same trailhead as nearby Overlooked Falls.
waterfalls.further: Check the park's South Boundary Road and Little Carp River Road conditions. The river crossing, mud and roots can change the difficulty after storms. Michigan DNR states South Boundary Road closes to vehicles at Headquarters Road south to the Pinkerton Trailhead from December 1 through late spring. The waterfall's normal visitor parking is on the affected park road system; do not plan an ordinary drive-up visit during that closure.
waterfalls.manager: Michigan DNR · Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
waterfalls.decision: Pick Greenstone for a short backcountry-feeling forest hike and a second possible waterfall stop at Overlooked Falls. This is not a drive-up waterfall.

waterfalls.name: Nonesuch Falls
waterfalls.walk: Follow the Nonesuch Mine historic walking trail past the old mine ruins toward the Little Iron River. Distances vary by route and viewpoint: allow a short woodland hike rather than assuming the falls are beside the parking area.
waterfalls.best: Spring or after recent rain, when the small bedrock ledges have more water; historic mining remains are also part of the experience.
waterfalls.access: Public state-park historic trail reached from a designated South Boundary Road parking area. The trail passes fragile 19th-century mine remains: leave stones, artifacts, foundation walls and old workings undisturbed.
waterfalls.note: Nonesuch Falls is a modest, roughly 10-foot series of rock ledges rather than a broad plunge. This stop pairs nature with copper-mining history.
waterfalls.parking: Use the Nonesuch Mine Trail parking area off South Boundary Road, identified by the Michigan DNR as N46°45.583′ W89°37.194′ (WGS84). The trailhead parking is north of the waterfall and distinct from its GIS point.
waterfalls.feature: A small Little Iron River waterfall beyond the preserved ruins of the historic Nonesuch copper mine.
waterfalls.further: Do not enter abandoned mine openings or climb masonry. Watch for unstable rock, unbridged wet sections and seasonal closures on South Boundary Road. Michigan DNR states South Boundary Road closes to vehicles at Headquarters Road south to the Pinkerton Trailhead from December 1 through late spring. The waterfall's normal visitor parking is on the affected park road system; do not plan an ordinary drive-up visit during that closure.
waterfalls.manager: Michigan DNR · Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
waterfalls.decision: Choose Nonesuch for a mine-history walk with a waterfall reward, not for waterfall height. Leave extra time to read signs and explore the designated historic trail.

landManager.description: Michigan DNR park maintains the Nonesuch historic mine and trail area

publicAccess.description: Michigan DNR park map marks Nonesuch Falls and the visitor walking route from South Boundary Road

parking.description: Michigan DNR official WGS84 waypoint: Nonesuch Parking N46°45.583′ W89°37.194′

trail.description: Michigan Trail Maps documents the historic Nonesuch Mine trail and Little Iron River waterfall access

waterfalls.name: Little Union Gorge Falls
waterfalls.walk: Walk the signed 1-mile Union Mine Interpretive Trail loop. Interpretive signs cover the 1846 copper mine; the trail passes the Little Union River gorge and several cascades. Keep to the established path instead of walking in the creek.
waterfalls.best: Spring melt and after rain make the multiple shallow river cascades most visible; fall brings color.
waterfalls.access: Public one-mile interpretive loop maintained by Michigan DNR in Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park. Road access, seasonal conditions, and park permit requirements are separate checks.
waterfalls.note: The interpretive loop is the product here: the little gorge, early copper-mining story and nearby water are all part of a useful stop. Low water can diminish the waterfall's spectacle.
waterfalls.parking: Use the signed Union Mine Interpretive Trail parking/trailhead on the west side of South Boundary Road, south of the Wilderness Visitor Center. Do not mistake the nearby outpost campground for the official trailhead.
waterfalls.feature: A string of modest gorge cascades within a signed one-mile loop through early copper-mining history.
waterfalls.further: The route is generally shorter than the park's backcountry trails, but wet rock and trail conditions still change after rain. Park in designated areas and stay out of river channels. Michigan DNR states South Boundary Road closes to vehicles at Headquarters Road south to the Pinkerton Trailhead from December 1 through late spring. The waterfall's normal visitor parking is on the affected park road system; do not plan an ordinary drive-up visit during that closure.
waterfalls.manager: Michigan DNR · Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
waterfalls.decision: Best short walk for combining several modest river drops with interpretive copper-mine history. It also works when a longer wilderness waterfall hike does not fit your day.

publicAccess.description: Michigan DNR trail guide identifies public Union Mine Interpretive Trail and Little Union gorge

waterfalls.name: Saxon Falls
waterfalls.walk: Follow the short wooded trail east of the Wisconsin-side parking area to Xcel Energy's provided overlook. Travel Wisconsin estimates 0.25–0.5 mile of gravel/dirt walking; the route is not described as wheelchair accessible.
waterfalls.best: After spring snowmelt or substantial rainfall, subject to hydroelectric regulation; no real-time discharge is offered.
waterfalls.access: Publicly described overlook reached ONLY from the Wisconsin bank of the Montreal River. Xcel Energy hydroelectric project land surrounds the falls; neither the Michigan bank nor the dam and gorge are general public access routes. Current visitor opening not established.
waterfalls.note: This fall is on a state-line river, but the documented visitor approach and overlook are in Wisconsin. Do not attempt river crossings, hydro plant approaches or a speculative Michigan-side trail.
waterfalls.parking: Use Wisconsin-side Saxon Falls Road (unpaved) and the signed overlook parking area at 46.535797, -90.380255. From US-2, use WI-122 to County Highway B, then Saxon Falls Road. Do not drive toward the Michigan GIS waterfall point.
waterfalls.feature: A powerful Montreal River cascade drops into a deep gorge near a working hydroelectric plant, with its safer public overlook reached from Wisconsin.
waterfalls.further: The access road is gravel, and seasonal road, ice, construction and hydro plant operating rules may change. Do not conflate Wisconsin DNR's public flowage boat landing with the waterfall overlook.
waterfalls.manager: Northern States Power Company–Wisconsin / Xcel Energy · Saxon Falls hydroelectric project
waterfalls.decision: Choose this border waterfall only when the Wisconsin-side overlook fits your itinerary. Superior Falls has a different, Michigan-side visitor entrance farther downstream.

landManager.description: Xcel Energy owns the project-boundary lands and operates Saxon Falls hydropower project

publicAccess.description: Community recreation authority describes Xcel Energy-provided overlook and specifies Wisconsin-bank-only safe approach

parking.description: Wisconsin signed Saxon Falls Road lot, listed at 46.535797, -90.380255; not the fall location

trail.description: Travel Wisconsin describes the developed footpath and 0.25–0.5 mile dirt/gravel visitor walking

waterfalls.manager: Michigan DNR · Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
waterfalls.winterRoad: Michigan DNR states that South Boundary Road is closed to ordinary vehicles from Headquarters Road south to Pinkerton Trailhead from December 1 through late spring. Neither a summer trailhead description nor a mapped waterfall confirms winter vehicle access.
waterfalls.name: Overlooked Falls
waterfalls.walk: From the signed Little Carp River Road trailhead, follow the Little Carp River Trail a few hundred feet to the first footbridge. Overlooked Falls is just downstream; check the bridge-side views without scrambling along the bank.
waterfalls.best: Spring snowmelt gives the small cascades more volume; moss and autumn color distinguish the shady river setting.
waterfalls.access: Public Michigan DNR state-park walking route from the Little Carp River Road lot. No water-flow or current road-opening data is supplied here.
waterfalls.parking: Signed Little Carp River Trailhead parking at the end of Little Carp River Road, entered from South Boundary Road. Use this lot, not the mapped waterfall coordinates.
waterfalls.feature: A short, quiet cascade a few hundred feet from the Little Carp River footbridge, an ideal introductory stop before the longer Greenstone Falls hike.
waterfalls.note: Overlooked Falls is beside the first bridge; Greenstone Falls is a separate waterfall farther along the same river trail. Do not mistake their pins or hiking distances.
waterfalls.decision: Pick Overlooked for the short stop from the Little Carp River parking area, then decide if you want to continue to Greenstone on the longer two-mile round-trip route.
waterfalls.further: The park's road system has seasonal vehicle closures. The footbridge and river stones can be wet and icy. Don't use this as a winter driving itinerary; check DNR conditions first.

landManager.description: Michigan DNR operates Porcupine Mountains and its Little Carp River Trail.

publicAccess.description: UP Travel identifies Overlooked Falls as a public state-park visitor stop reached from the Little Carp River trailhead.

parking.description: Western UP visitor guidance identifies the signed parking at the end of Little Carp River Road from South Boundary Road.

trail.description: From the lot, Overlooked Falls lies a few hundred feet down the Little Carp River Trail by the first footbridge.

location.description: Michigan state GIS #97 maps the waterfall, not visitor parking.

waterfalls.name: Trap Falls
waterfalls.walk: Take the Government Peak Trail from its signed M-107 trailhead. Michigan DNR's visitor publication describes a 3.2-mile round-trip hike to Trap Falls; other guides publish longer approaches. Confirm the current route and mileage on the DNR trail map before leaving the trailhead.
waterfalls.best: Spring and late summer after rain, with added interest from remote old-growth river scenery.
waterfalls.access: Public nonmotorized Government Peak Trail within Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park. This is a committed woodland hike, not a pullout or accessible waterfall platform.
waterfalls.parking: Use the designated Government Peak Trailhead parking on M-107 inside Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park. Do not navigate to the waterfall coordinate or improvise riverbank parking.
waterfalls.feature: A remote Upper Carp River cascade reached on a sustained Government Peak Trail walk through rugged Porcupine Mountains forest.
waterfalls.note: Route mileage differs among DNR and regional descriptions; this guide deliberately follows the DNR visitor publication while warning visitors to verify current signage.
waterfalls.decision: Choose Trap Falls for a half-day hiking destination rather than a quick scenic stop. Compare with Overlooked if your party needs a much shorter walk.
waterfalls.further: The river corridor has roots, grades, potential mud and slippery rock. Do not attempt the falls as a casual winter stop or assume water crossings are bridged. M-107 and South Boundary Road seasonal restrictions may affect driving access.

landManager.description: Michigan DNR manages the Government Peak Trail and Upper Carp River corridor.

publicAccess.description: Michigan DNR identifies Trap Falls as a public day-hike destination from Government Peak Trailhead.

parking.description: The DNR visitor publication identifies the designated Government Peak Trailhead on M-107 as the starting point.

trail.description: DNR identifies a 3.2-mile round-trip hiking route; another regional guide uses a different mileage, so current signs should be checked.

location.description: Michigan state GIS waterfall #118 maps the river drop, not the M-107 parking area.

waterfalls.name: Cascade Falls
waterfalls.walk: From the signed parking area on Forest Road 468, take the established Cascade Falls main trail about 0.75 mile one way. The optional Bluff Trail is about one mile one way, considerably rougher and involves scrambling.
waterfalls.best: Snow-free hiking conditions, when forest roads are passable; spring water and autumn colors can be rewarding.
waterfalls.access: Public trail on Ottawa National Forest land. The December 2025 North Country Trail Association guide confirms the signed parking on FR 468, but the proposed North Country Trail connector is not a completed official trail.
waterfalls.note: This is Cascade Falls on Cascade Creek in the Trap Hills near Bergland, not the unrelated Cascade Falls in Utah or Jackson, Michigan. Michigan GIS #67 marks the falls, not the parking lot.
waterfalls.parking: Drive to the signed Cascade Falls Trail parking area on Forest Road 468 after turning off Forest Road 400 near Bergland. Use the posted trailhead, never the mapped waterfall point as a driving destination.
waterfalls.feature: A forest cascade hidden among rugged Trap Hills rock, reached by a straightforward main trail or a more demanding ridge-loop alternative.
waterfalls.decision: Choose the main trail for the waterfall with a moderate forest walk. Choose the longer Bluff Trail only if you want rocky ridge terrain and are comfortable scrambling.
waterfalls.further: Forest roads in this area are not plowed in winter, and snowmelt/road damage can make access impossible even after the snow is gone. No live trail-opening, road, ice or water-flow status is supplied.
waterfalls.manager: USDA Forest Service · Ottawa National Forest
waterfalls.winterRoad: The NCTA's December 2025 guide says surrounding forest access roads are unplowed in winter and often need drying after snowmelt. The FR 468 signed lot is a mapped summer trailhead, not a winter road-open promise.

landManager.description: December 2025 Peter Wolfe Chapter guide lists Forest Service ownership and Ottawa National Forest responsibility for Cascade Falls spur-trail maintenance.

publicAccess.description: Official USDA Forest Service Trap Hills brochure describes the signed public Cascade Falls Trail; NCTA 2025 guide corroborates it.

parking.description: December 2025 NCTA PDF page 11 (printed source page 11) visibly identifies signed Cascade Falls Trail parking at FR 468, separate from the waterfall and proposed connector.

trail.description: The Forest Service identifies 0.75 mile one way for main trail and one mile one way for the difficult Bluff Trail. NCTA 2025 identifies the existing FR468 route as established.

location.description: Michigan state GIS feature #67 at 46.651708, -89.446195 places Cascade Falls on Cascade Creek; this is not a vehicle parking coordinate.

waterfalls.name: Bonanza Falls (Greenwood Falls)
waterfalls.place: Greenwoods Township Park · Big Iron River
waterfalls.walk: From the signed Greenwoods township park parking area off M-64, follow the short established path to the upper river viewing area, then return the same way. This is NOT an authorized route to every downstream waterfall or riverbank section; no surveyed trail line or exact length is claimed.
waterfalls.best: Snow-free park season with flowing water; spring after rain can bring stronger water, while fall foliage frames the river shelves.
waterfalls.access: Carp Lake Township explicitly lists Greenwoods (Bonanza Falls) as a public park with falls and provides its own map directions; a separate local guide documents the direct signed visitor path from the lot to the upper falls. Do not cross unmarked parcels or follow the river downstream on an assumed public path.
waterfalls.parking: Follow Carp Lake Township's published Greenwoods (Bonanza Falls) destination off M-64 south of Silver City. Use the actual signed gravel park entrance and designated parking lot. The township's Google Maps link gives a park destination area, NOT a surveyed lot coordinate; NEVER route to the waterfall GIS #124 pin.
waterfalls.feature: Broad layered cascades and multiple low drops on the Big Iron River. The easily visited upper falls are approached through the signed Greenwoods township park rather than directly from the geographic waterfall coordinate.
waterfalls.note: Three separate references: land-manager Google Maps park destination (46.8176942,-89.5674561), regional upper-falls reference (46.817719,-89.570023) in township-attributed land, and MI GIS natural falls #124 (46.818863,-89.571458) on a separately attributed parcel. These are NOT interchangeable directions. No surveyed pedestrian path or easement to downstream drops is established.
waterfalls.decision: Choose Bonanza for a short signed township-park upper-falls stop only when its seasonal entrance is open. Follow the established path from the public lot to river views, then turn around; do not extend the hike along the falls GIS location.
waterfalls.further: Carp Lake Township 2025 meeting minutes describe seasonal park closure toward winter; no 2026 closing date or open-now status is verified. The short walk is natural and rocky, with slippery water-worn ledges and no documented accessible platform. Neither brochure coordinates nor parcel polygons authorize crossing private river frontage.
waterfalls.manager: Carp Lake Township · Greenwoods (Bonanza Falls) park
waterfalls.winterRoad: Carp Lake Township records weather-dependent late-fall closure and closure through winter in 2025, but does not publish a verified 2026 schedule in sources checked. A published summer map pin cannot establish winter parking or a current open gate.

landManager.description: Carp Lake Township's own Parks & Facilities directory identifies Greenwoods (Bonanza Falls) as a township-managed park with falls and directions.
